One ifrit of the devils said: "I have been given such strength that, if I wish, I can turn into a fiery whirlwind and burn everything I pass over." Iblis said to him: "Go to the camels and their herders." So he came to the camels when they had lowered their heads and settled in their pastures. People did not notice until a fiery whirlwind erupted from beneath the earth; no one approached it without being burned. It burned the camels and their herders until it reached the last of them. Then the enemy of Allah, Iblis, came in an ugly form, riding a camel, to Job, and found him standing and praying. He said: "O Job, a fire came and enveloped your camels and burned them, and everyone among them except me." Job said: "Praise be to Allah, who gave them and who took them. Long ago I accustomed my wealth and myself to perishing." Iblis said: "Your Lord sent down a fire from the sky upon them, and it burned them, leaving the people bewildered and amazed at it. Some of them say: 'Job did not worship anything, and he was only in delusion.' Others say: 'If Job's god were able to do anything, he would have protected his ally [wali]' [[In "b": "an ʿan waliyyihi Ayyub" (from his ally Job).]]. And others say: 'Rather, it was he who did it, to gloat over his enemy and grieve his friend.'"

Job said: "Praise be to Allah when He gave me and when He took from me. I came out naked from my mother's womb, and naked I will return to the earth, and naked I will be gathered to Allah. It is not for you to rejoice when He lent you, nor to grieve when He took back His loan from you. Allah has more right over you and over what He gave you. Had Allah known any good in you, O servant, He would have taken your soul with those souls and you would have become a martyr. But He knew evil in you, so He delayed you." Iblis returned to his companions [defeated] [[Addition from "b".]], humiliated and disgraced, and said to them: "What strength do you have? For I did not affect his heart?" An ifrit said: "I have such strength that, whenever I wish, I can let out a cry that no living soul hears without its life-breath leaving it." Iblis said: "Go to the sheep and their shepherds." So he went until he reached the middle of them, then cried out one cry, and they all collapsed dead, and their shepherd died. Then Iblis came, disguised as the steward of the shepherds, to Job while he was praying. He said to him the same first words, and Job answered him the same first answer. Then Iblis returned to his companions and said: "What strength do you have? For I did not affect Job's heart." An ifrit said: "I have such strength that, if I wish, I can turn into a violent wind that uproots everything it passes over." He said: "Go to the plowmen and the fields." So he went, and they did not notice until a violent wind blew and uprooted everything of theirs until it was as if it had never been. Then Iblis came, disguised as the steward of the field, to Job while he was standing and praying. He said to him the same first words, and Job answered him the same answer as his first reply. Whenever the destruction of one of his properties was reported to him, he praised Allah and spoke His praise in the best manner, and he was content with the decree and resolved to endure the trial patiently, until no wealth remained to him.

When Iblis saw that he had destroyed his wealth, he ascended to the sky and said: "My God, Job thinks that You did not grant him enjoyment through his children; You gave him wealth, so will You let me have power over his children? For it is a calamity before which the hearts of men cannot stand." Allah, Exalted is He, said:

"Go, for I have given you power over his children." So the enemy of Allah swooped down until he came to the sons of Job while they were in their palace. He kept shaking them until the palace collapsed from its foundations. Then he began to strike its walls against one another and pelt them with wood and stones, until he had mutilated them in every way. He lifted the palace and overturned it, so they became upside down. Then he went to Job disguised as the teacher who used to instruct them in wisdom, but he was wounded in the face, his blood and brain flowing, and he informed him, saying:

"If you had seen your sons, how they were tortured and overturned, lying upside down on their heads with their blood and brains flowing, and if you had seen how their bellies were split open and their intestines scattered, your heart would have been cut in pieces." He kept saying this and similar things until Job softened, wept, took a handful of dust and placed it on his head, and said:

"Would that my mother had not borne me!" Iblis seized upon that and ascended swiftly with the news of Job's distress, delighted with it. Then Job did not delay before he returned to himself, saw clearly, and sought forgiveness, and his companions among the angels ascended with his repentance, so his repentance reached Allah before (anything else), and Allah knows best. Iblis stood humiliated and said:

"My God, what made Job's loss of wealth and children easy for him was that he saw from You that You had not granted him enjoyment of his own body. So You restore to him wealth and children; will You then let me have power over his body?"

Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said:

"Go, for I have given you power over his body, but you have no power over his tongue or his heart." Allah, Exalted and Mighty, knew of him; He gave power over him only as a mercy to him, to magnify his reward, to make him a lesson for the patient and a reminder for worshippers in every trial that befalls them, so that they might take him as an example in patience and hope for reward. The enemy of Allah swooped down swiftly and found Job prostrating, so he hastened before he raised his head, came at him from the front of his face, and blew into his nostril a blast by which his entire body caught fire. There emerged from his horn to his foot boils like the rumps of sheep, and an itching fell upon him, so he scratched himself with his nails until they all fell off; then he scratched with coarse hair-cloths until he cut them, then he scratched with pottery and rough stones. He kept scratching until his flesh festered, broke apart, changed, and stank. The people of the village removed him and placed him on a refuse heap, and made him a shelter. All of Allah's creatures abandoned him except his wife, Rahmah daughter of Ifrathim son of Yusuf son of Yaqub, who used to come to him to tend to what he needed and attend to him. When the three of his companions, namely Yaqin, Yaldad and Safir, saw what Allah had afflicted him with, they accused him and abandoned him, without leaving his religion. When the affliction lengthened, they went to him, rebuked him, blamed him, and said to him:

"Repent to Allah of the sin for which you have been punished." He said:

A young man who was of recent age and had believed in him and affirmed him was present with them, and he said to them:

"You have spoken, O elders, and you were more entitled to speak than I because of your ages. But you have left aside a better word than the one you spoke, a more correct opinion than the one you held, and a more fitting course than the one you took. Job had more right and claim upon you than what you have described. So do you know, O elders, whose right you have violated, whose sanctity you have transgressed, and who is the man you have blamed and accused?"

Did you not know that Ayyub was the Prophet of Allah, His chosen one among His creation and His elite among the people of the earth up to this day of yours? Then you did not know, and Allah did not inform you of His affair, that He had become angry with him in any matter since He gave him what He gave him until this day of yours, nor that He had taken from him any of the honour with which He had honoured him, nor that Ayyub said anything about Allah other than the truth throughout the time you accompanied him until this day of yours. So if it is affliction that has belittled him in your eyes and lowered him in your souls, then you know that Allah tests the believers, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous, and His testing of them is no proof of His anger toward them nor of their humiliation, but it is honour and a favour for them. If Ayyub were not, in Allah's sight, at this rank, but were only a brother whom you loved for the sake of companionship, it would not be fitting for the forbearing man to blame his brother at the time of affliction, nor to reproach him with calamity, nor to disparage him with what he does not know while he is distressed and grieved. Rather, he would have mercy on him, weep with him, ask forgiveness for him, grieve at his grief, and guide him to the right paths of his affair. Whoever is ignorant of this is neither forbearing nor rightly guided. So, fear Allah, fear Allah, O elders, though in the greatness and majesty of Allah and the remembrance of death there is what cuts out your tongues and breaks your hearts. Did you not know that Allah has servants whom fear has silenced, not from inability or muteness, and that they are eloquent, articulate, noble, wise, and the scholars of Allah? But when they remember the greatness of Allah, their tongues are cut off, their skins shiver, their hearts break, and their minds are bewildered, out of magnifying and revering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When they recover from that, they hasten toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with pure deeds, considering themselves among the wrongdoers and sinners, though they are truly righteous and innocent, and among the negligent and remiss, though they are truly intelligent and strong. Then Ayyub said:

Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sows wisdom with mercy in the heart of the young and the old. When it takes root in the heart, Allah makes it manifest upon the tongue. Wisdom does not come from age, grey hair, or long experience. When Allah makes a servant wise in youth, his standing is not diminished among the wise, and they see upon him, from Allah, the Glorified, the light of honour. Then Ayyub turned away from them and turned to his Lord, seeking refuge in Him and humbling himself before Him, and said: "My Lord, for what purpose did You create me? Would that I had not been created, since You have come to hate me! Would that I had known the sin I committed and the deed I did, so that You turned Your noble face away from me! If only You had caused me to die and joined me to my noble fathers, then death would have been more fitting for me. Was I not a home for the stranger, a shelter for the poor, a guardian for the orphan, and a protector for the widow? My God, I am Your servant: if I do good, then the favour is Yours, and if I do evil, then my punishment is in Your hand. You have made me a target and a stake for trials. Affliction has fallen upon me which, if You had imposed it upon a mountain, it would have been too weak to bear, so how can my weakness bear it? Indeed Your decree is what has humbled me, and Your dominion is what has sickened me and wasted my body. If my Lord were to remove the awe that is in my breast and loosen my tongue so that I could speak with full mouth of what it befits a servant to argue in his own defence, I would hope that He would then heal me of what I suffer. But He has cast me off and has turned away from me. He sees me, and I do not see Him; He hears me, and I do not hear Him. He does not look upon me so as to have mercy on me, nor does He draw near to me or bring me near, so that I might present my excuse, speak of my innocence, and dispute on my own behalf."

When Ayyub and his companions were with him and he said this, a cloud overshadowed him until his companions thought it was a painful punishment. Then he was called: "O Ayyub, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says:

Behold, I have drawn near to you, and I have never been far from you. Arise, present your excuse, speak of your innocence, dispute on your own behalf, gird up your loins, and stand as a mighty one disputing with a mighty one, if you are able. For none should dispute with Me except one mighty like Me. Your soul has deceived you, O Ayyub, into a matter that your strength cannot reach. Where were you when I created the earth and laid it on its foundation? Were you with Me, extending its edges? Did you know by what measure I determined it, or upon what I set its sides? Did water carry the earth by your obedience, or was the earth a covering for the water by Your wisdom? Where were you when I raised the sky as a roof in the air, not suspended by any cause from above, nor supported by any prop from below? Did your wisdom reach the point of making its light flow, or of moving its stars, or of making its night and day alternate by your command? Where were you when We sent forth the rivers and the seas were filled? Did your power restrain the waves of the seas within their boundaries? Or did your power open the wombs when their term was fulfilled? Where were you when I poured water upon the dust and set up the towering mountains? Do you know upon what I fixed them? By what weight did I weigh them? Or do you have an arm that can bear them? Or do you know from where the water comes that I send down from the sky? Or do you know from what I create the clouds? Or do you know where the treasuries of snow are? Or where are the mountains of hail? Or where is the store-house of the night by day [and the store-house of the day by night]? And where is the store-house of the wind? And in what language do the trees speak? And who placed intellects in the chests of men? And who split hearing and sight? And who made the angels submissive to His kingdom, and subdued the tyrants by His might? And who apportioned the provisions by His wisdom?"

This was in a long discourse of the signs of His power that He mentioned to Ayyub. Then Ayyub said:

"My station has become small, and all my tongue, my intellect and my understanding have been brought low, and my strength has grown weak before this matter that confronts me, O my God. I know that all that You have mentioned is the handiwork of Your hands and the governance of Your wisdom, and greater and more wondrous than that, and if You willed, You would act. Nothing can overpower You, and nothing is hidden from You, since affliction has come upon me. O my God, I spoke, and I did not control my tongue, and affliction was what made me speak. Would that the earth had split open for me so that I might go into it, and not have spoken anything that angers my Lord. Would that I had died of my grief in the severest of my trials before this. I spoke only so that You would excuse me, and I was silent only so that You would have mercy on me. A word slipped from me, and I will not return to it. I have placed my hand upon my mouth, bitten my tongue, and pressed my cheek into the dust. I seek refuge in You today from You, and I ask You to protect me from the severity of the affliction, so protect me. I seek Your help against Your punishment, so help me. I seek Your aid in my affair, so aid me. I rely upon You, so suffice me. I hold fast to You, so preserve me. And [I say to my wife]: you did not act justly. Had you been patient in affliction for eighty years as we were in ease for eighty years... By Allah, if Allah heals me, I will flog you one hundred lashes, because you commanded me to slaughter for other than Allah. Your food and your drink that you brought me are forbidden to me [or: it is forbidden to me] to taste anything of what you bring me after you said this to me. So go away from me, and I will not see you." So he drove her away, and she left. When Ayyub looked, and there was no food, no drink and no friend with him, he fell down in prostration and said:

﴿My Lord, indeed harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾

It was said to him: "Lift your head, for your prayer has been answered. Strike with your foot." He struck with his foot, and a spring gushed forth, and he bathed in it, and no outward trace of his disease remained except that it fell away, and his youth and beauty returned to him better than they had been. Then he struck with his foot again, and another spring gushed forth, and he drank from it, and no disease remained in his belly except that it came out. He stood up healthy and was clothed in a fine garment.

He began to look around, and he saw nothing of what he had possessed of family and wealth except that Allah had multiplied it for him. By Allah, it has been reported to us that the water in which he bathed scattered upon his chest as golden locusts, and he began to gather them in his hand. Then Allah revealed to him: "O Ayyub, did I not make you rich?" He said: "Yes, but this is Your blessing; who could be satisfied with it?" He went out and sat in an elevated place. Then his wife said: "Do you see? If he had driven me away to someone who would feed him? Shall I leave him to die of hunger and be lost, so that the beasts devour him?" She returned to him, but found no dung-heap and no state that she had known, and matters had changed. She began to wander where the dung-heap had been, weeping, and that was in Ayyub's sight. She was afraid of the man in the fine garment to approach him and ask him about him. So Ayyub called her and said:

"What do you want, O servant of Allah?"

She wept and said: "I wanted that afflicted man who was cast away on the dung-heap. I do not know whether he has perished or what has become of him." Ayyub said: "What was that from you?" She wept and said: "My husband." He said: "Would you recognise him if you saw him?" She said: "Could anyone who has seen him be hidden from me?" Then she began to look at him while being in awe of him, and then she said: "Surely he resembles most of Allah's creation to you when he was healthy." He said: "Indeed I am Ayyub, whom you commanded me to slaughter for Iblis. I obeyed Allah, disobeyed Satan, and called upon Allah, the Glorified, and He returned to me what you see."

Wahb said: Ayyub remained in affliction for three years. When Ayyub overcame Iblis and Iblis could not gain anything from him, Iblis appeared to his wife in a form unlike the form of the children of Adam in size, body, and beauty, upon a mount unlike the mounts of people, having greatness, splendor, and perfection. He said to her: "Are you the wife of Ayyub, this afflicted man?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know me?" She said: "No." He said: "I am the god of the earth, and I am the one who did to your companion what I did, because he worshipped the god of the heavens and left me, and so he angered me. If he had prostrated to me one single prostration, I would have returned to him and to you all the wealth and children you had, for it is with me." Then he showed them to her in the valley bottom where she had met him. Wahb said: I have also heard that he only said to her: "If your companion had eaten food without mentioning the name of Allah over it, he would have been healed of the affliction he has." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 17/66-67.]] And Allah knows best.

It is mentioned in some books that Iblis said to her: "Prostrate to me one prostration, and I will return to you the wealth and the children and heal your husband." She returned to Ayyub and informed him of what he had said to her [and what he had shown her]. [[Omitted from "B".]] He said: "The enemy of Allah has come to you to tempt you away from your religion." Then he swore that if Allah healed him, he would strike her one hundred lashes. At that point he said: "Harm has touched me" [referring to] Iblis's greed for her prostration to him, which violated my sanctity, and his calling her and me to disbelief. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, had mercy on Ayyub's wife for her patience with him in the affliction, and lightened it for her. He also wished to fulfil Ayyub's oath, so He commanded him to take a bundle containing one hundred small twigs and strike her with it in one blow, as Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it, and do not break your oath﴾ (38:44). It is also related that Iblis made a chest and put medicines in it, and sat on the road of his wife, treating people. Ayyub's wife passed by him and said: "[O shaykh], I have a sick man; shall I bring him to be treated?" He said: "Yes, [by Allah], I want nothing except that he say, when I have cured him, 'You have cured me.'" She mentioned this to Ayyub, and he said: "It is Iblis who has deceived you," and he swore that if Allah healed him, he would strike her one hundred lashes.

Wahb and others said: Ayyub's wife used to work for people and bring him his sustenance. When the affliction lengthened upon him and people grew weary of him, and no one employed her, she sought, one day, something to feed him, but found nothing. So she cut off a lock from her head and sold it for a loaf of bread and brought it to him. He said to her: "Where is your lock?" She informed him. [[Mentioned by al-Tabari: 17/66, from Wahb ibn Munabbih.]] At that point he said: ﴿Harm has touched me﴾.

Some people said: He only said that when worms reached his heart and tongue, and he feared they would make him cease from remembrance and reflection.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: He did not call upon Allah to remove it from him until three things had become apparent to him. The first: two friends came to him when news of him reached them; they came to him, and nothing remained of him except his eyes, and they saw a great matter, and said: "If you had a standing with Allah, this would not have befallen you." The second: his wife asked for food and found nothing to feed him, so she sold her forelock and brought him food. The third: Iblis's saying, "I will treat him on condition that he says, 'You have cured me.'"

It was also said: Iblis whispered to him that his wife had committed adultery, so she cut off her forelock. At that point his patience was overwhelmed, so he prayed and swore that he would strike her one hundred lashes. It was also said: its meaning is ﴿Harm has touched me﴾ from the gloating of enemies, to the extent that it is related that after he was healed he was asked: "What was harder for you in your affliction?" He said: "The gloating of the enemies." It was also said: he said that when a worm fell from his thigh and he put it back in its place.

[And he said: "Eat, for Allah has made me your food,"] so she bit him a bite whose pain exceeded everything he had suffered from the biting of the worms.

If it is said: Allah called him "patient," yet he displayed complaint and distress, by his saying: ﴿Indeed, harm has touched me﴾ and ﴿Satan has touched me with hardship and torment﴾ (38:41). It is said: this is not complaint; rather it is supplication, as evidenced by the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿So We responded to him﴾ (21:84). Moreover, distress is only in complaining to creatures; as for complaining to Allah, mighty and majestic, it is not distress nor abandonment of patience, as Ya'qub said: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah﴾ (12:86). Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: Likewise, whoever displays complaint to people while being content with the decree of Allah, this is not distress, as it is related that Jibril entered upon the Prophet ﷺ during his illness and said: "How do you find yourself?" He said: "I find myself troubled, and I find myself distressed." [[A fragment from a long hadith narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 3/139. al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 9/35, "In its chain is 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, who is abandoned in hadith."]]

And he said to 'A'isha when she said, "Oh my head!": "Nay, rather I say, 'Oh my head!'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Patients, chapter: What is permitted for the patient to say: "I have pain," or "Oh my head!"...: 10/123.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 82–83 (part 1 of 3):

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And of the devils﴾, meaning: We subjected to him some of the devils, ﴿who dived for him﴾, meaning: they would enter beneath the water and bring forth for him jewels from the depths of the sea, ﴿and did other work besides that﴾, meaning: other than diving, which is what Allah, Exalted is He, mentioned: ﴿They made for him whatever he willed of prayer niches and statues﴾ (Saba': 13), and so on.

﴿And We were watching over them﴾, so that they would not go out from His command. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, "We kept them safe from spoiling what they had done." In the narrative, Sulayman, when he sent a devil with a man to do a task for him, would say to him: "If he finishes his work before night, keep him busy with another task so that he does not spoil what he has done." It was the habit of the devils that, when they finished their work and were not occupied with another task, they would destroy and spoil what they had done.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And Job, when he called out to his Lord﴾, meaning: he supplicated his Lord. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Job (peace be upon him) was a man from the Romans; he was Job son of Amos son of Razikh son of Rum son of Eis son of Isaac son of Abraham. His mother was from the descendants of Lot son of Haran. Allah had chosen him, made him a prophet, and spread the world out for him. He had al-BatanIyya in the land of Sham, all of it, its plains and its mountains, and he had in it every kind of wealth: cattle, camels, sheep, horses and donkeys, in a quantity and abundance that no other man could surpass. He had five hundred plows, each followed by five hundred servants, and every servant had a wife, a child and property. The equipment of each plow was carried by a she-ass that bore young, two, three, four, five or more. Allah, Exalted is He, had given him family and children, men and women. He was pious, righteous, merciful to the poor; he fed the needy, sponsored widows and orphans, honored the guest and gave to the wayfarer. He was grateful for Allah's blessings and fulfilled Allah's right. He was protected from the enemy of Allah, Iblis, from reaching him in the way he reaches the wealthy through heedlessness, negligence and being preoccupied with worldly things away from the command of Allah. He had three companions who believed in him and affirmed him: a man from the people of Yemen called Yaqin, and two men from one town, one of whom was called Yaldad and the other Safir. They were middle-aged. Iblis could not be barred from any of the heavens, and he would stand in them wherever he wished, until Allah raised Jesus, after which he was barred from four heavens. When Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, he was barred from the remaining three. Iblis heard the angels responding with prayers upon Job, at the time Allah mentioned him and praised him. Envy and resentment seized him, so he ascended swiftly until he stood at a place in the sky where he used to stand, and said: "My God, I considered the affair of Your servant Job and found him a servant whom You favored, and he thanked You; You granted him health and he praised You. If You were to test him by taking away what You gave him, he would change from his state of thankfulness and worship to You, and he would depart from Your obedience." Allah, Exalted is He, said: "Go, for I have given you power over his property." So the enemy of Allah, Iblis, swooped down until he landed on the earth. Then he gathered the ifrits of the jinn and the rebellious devils and said to them: "What strength do you have? For I have been given power over the property of Job." That is a dreadful calamity and a trial that men cannot endure. One ifrit of the devils said: "I have been given such strength that, if I wish, I can turn into a fiery whirlwind and burn everything I pass over." Iblis said to him: "Go to the camels and their herders." So he came to the camels when they had lowered their heads and settled in their pastures. People did not notice until a fiery whirlwind erupted from beneath the earth; no one approached it without being burned. It burned the camels and their herders until it reached the last of them. Then the enemy of Allah, Iblis, came in an ugly form, riding a camel, to Job, and found him standing and praying. He said: "O Job, a fire came and enveloped your camels and burned them, and everyone among them except me." Job said: "Praise be to Allah, who gave them and who took them. Long ago I accustomed my wealth and myself to perishing." Iblis said: "Your Lord sent down a fire from the sky upon them, and it burned them, leaving the people bewildered and amazed at it. Some of them say: 'Job did not worship anything, and he was only in delusion.' Others say: 'If Job's god were able to do anything, he would have protected his ally [wali]' [[In "b": "an ʿan waliyyihi Ayyub" (from his ally Job).]]. And others say: 'Rather, it was he who did it, to gloat over his enemy and grieve his friend.'"

Job said: "Praise be to Allah when He gave me and when He took from me. I came out naked from my mother's womb, and naked I will return to the earth, and naked I will be gathered to Allah. It is not for you to rejoice when He lent you, nor to grieve when He took back His loan from you. Allah has more right over you and over what He gave you. Had Allah known any good in you, O servant, He would have taken your soul with those souls and you would have become a martyr. But He knew evil in you, so He delayed you." Iblis returned to his companions [defeated] [[Addition from "b".]], humiliated and disgraced, and said to them: "What strength do you have? For I did not affect his heart?" An ifrit said: "I have such strength that, whenever I wish, I can let out a cry that no living soul hears without its life-breath leaving it." Iblis said: "Go to the sheep and their shepherds." So he went until he reached the middle of them, then cried out one cry, and they all collapsed dead, and their shepherd died. Then Iblis came, disguised as the steward of the shepherds, to Job while he was praying. He said to him the same first words, and Job answered him the same first answer. Then Iblis returned to his companions and said: "What strength do you have? For I did not affect Job's heart." An ifrit said: "I have such strength that, if I wish, I can turn into a violent wind that uproots everything it passes over." He said: "Go to the plowmen and the fields." So he went, and they did not notice until a violent wind blew and uprooted everything of theirs until it was as if it had never been. Then Iblis came, disguised as the steward of the field, to Job while he was standing and praying. He said to him the same first words, and Job answered him the same answer as his first reply. Whenever the destruction of one of his properties was reported to him, he praised Allah and spoke His praise in the best manner, and he was content with the decree and resolved to endure the trial patiently, until no wealth remained to him.

When Iblis saw that he had destroyed his wealth, he ascended to the sky and said: "My God, Job thinks that You did not grant him enjoyment through his children; You gave him wealth, so will You let me have power over his children? For it is a calamity before which the hearts of men cannot stand." Allah, Exalted is He, said:

"Go, for I have given you power over his children." So the enemy of Allah swooped down until he came to the sons of Job while they were in their palace. He kept shaking them until the palace collapsed from its foundations. Then he began to strike its walls against one another and pelt them with wood and stones, until he had mutilated them in every way. He lifted the palace and overturned it, so they became upside down. Then he went to Job disguised as the teacher who used to instruct them in wisdom, but he was wounded in the face, his blood and brain flowing, and he informed him, saying:

"If you had seen your sons, how they were tortured and overturned, lying upside down on their heads with their blood and brains flowing, and if you had seen how their bellies were split open and their intestines scattered, your heart would have been cut in pieces." He kept saying this and similar things until Job softened, wept, took a handful of dust and placed it on his head, and said:

"Would that my mother had not borne me!" Iblis seized upon that and ascended swiftly with the news of Job's distress, delighted with it. Then Job did not delay before he returned to himself, saw clearly, and sought forgiveness, and his companions among the angels ascended with his repentance, so his repentance reached Allah before (anything else), and Allah knows best. Iblis stood humiliated and said:

"My God, what made Job's loss of wealth and children easy for him was that he saw from You that You had not granted him enjoyment of his own body. So You restore to him wealth and children; will You then let me have power over his body?"

Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said:

"Go, for I have given you power over his body, but you have no power over his tongue or his heart." Allah, Exalted and Mighty, knew of him; He gave power over him only as a mercy to him, to magnify his reward, to make him a lesson for the patient and a reminder for worshippers in every trial that befalls them, so that they might take him as an example in patience and hope for reward. The enemy of Allah swooped down swiftly and found Job prostrating, so he hastened before he raised his head, came at him from the front of his face, and blew into his nostril a blast by which his entire body caught fire. There emerged from his horn to his foot boils like the rumps of sheep, and an itching fell upon him, so he scratched himself with his nails until they all fell off; then he scratched with coarse hair-cloths until he cut them, then he scratched with pottery and rough stones. He kept scratching until his flesh festered, broke apart, changed, and stank. The people of the village removed him and placed him on a refuse heap, and made him a shelter. All of Allah's creatures abandoned him except his wife, Rahmah daughter of Ifrathim son of Yusuf son of Yaqub, who used to come to him to tend to what he needed and attend to him. When the three of his companions, namely Yaqin, Yaldad and Safir, saw what Allah had afflicted him with, they accused him and abandoned him, without leaving his religion. When the affliction lengthened, they went to him, rebuked him, blamed him, and said to him:

"Repent to Allah of the sin for which you have been punished." He said:

A young man who was of recent age and had believed in him and affirmed him was present with them, and he said to them:

"You have spoken, O elders, and you were more entitled to speak than I because of your ages. But you have left aside a better word than the one you spoke, a more correct opinion than the one you held, and a more fitting course than the one you took. Job had more right and claim upon you than what you have described. So do you know, O elders, whose right you have violated, whose sanctity you have transgressed, and who is the man you have blamed and accused?"

Did you not know that Ayyub was the Prophet of Allah, His chosen one among His creation and His elite among the people of the earth up to this day of yours? Then you did not know, and Allah did not inform you of His affair, that He had become angry with him in any matter since He gave him what He gave him until this day of yours, nor that He had taken from him any of the honour with which He had honoured him, nor that Ayyub said anything about Allah other than the truth throughout the time you accompanied him until this day of yours. So if it is affliction that has belittled him in your eyes and lowered him in your souls, then you know that Allah tests the believers, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous, and His testing of them is no proof of His anger toward them nor of their humiliation, but it is honour and a favour for them. If Ayyub were not, in Allah's sight, at this rank, but were only a brother whom you loved for the sake of companionship, it would not be fitting for the forbearing man to blame his brother at the time of affliction, nor to reproach him with calamity, nor to disparage him with what he does not know while he is distressed and grieved. Rather, he would have mercy on him, weep with him, ask forgiveness for him, grieve at his grief, and guide him to the right paths of his affair. Whoever is ignorant of this is neither forbearing nor rightly guided. So, fear Allah, fear Allah, O elders, though in the greatness and majesty of Allah and the remembrance of death there is what cuts out your tongues and breaks your hearts. Did you not know that Allah has servants whom fear has silenced, not from inability or muteness, and that they are eloquent, articulate, noble, wise, and the scholars of Allah? But when they remember the greatness of Allah, their tongues are cut off, their skins shiver, their hearts break, and their minds are bewildered, out of magnifying and revering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When they recover from that, they hasten toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with pure deeds, considering themselves among the wrongdoers and sinners, though they are truly righteous and innocent, and among the negligent and remiss, though they are truly intelligent and strong. Then Ayyub said:

Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sows wisdom with mercy in the heart of the young and the old. When it takes root in the heart, Allah makes it manifest upon the tongue. Wisdom does not come from age, grey hair, or long experience. When Allah makes a servant wise in youth, his standing is not diminished among the wise, and they see upon him, from Allah, the Glorified, the light of honour. Then Ayyub turned away from them and turned to his Lord, seeking refuge in Him and humbling himself before Him, and said: "My Lord, for what purpose did You create me? Would that I had not been created, since You have come to hate me! Would that I had known the sin I committed and the deed I did, so that You turned Your noble face away from me! If only You had caused me to die and joined me to my noble fathers, then death would have been more fitting for me. Was I not a home for the stranger, a shelter for the poor, a guardian for the orphan, and a protector for the widow? My God, I am Your servant: if I do good, then the favour is Yours, and if I do evil, then my punishment is in Your hand. You have made me a target and a stake for trials. Affliction has fallen upon me which, if You had imposed it upon a mountain, it would have been too weak to bear, so how can my weakness bear it? Indeed Your decree is what has humbled me, and Your dominion is what has sickened me and wasted my body. If my Lord were to remove the awe that is in my breast and loosen my tongue so that I could speak with full mouth of what it befits a servant to argue in his own defence, I would hope that He would then heal me of what I suffer. But He has cast me off and has turned away from me. He sees me, and I do not see Him; He hears me, and I do not hear Him. He does not look upon me so as to have mercy on me, nor does He draw near to me or bring me near, so that I might present my excuse, speak of my innocence, and dispute on my own behalf."

When Ayyub and his companions were with him and he said this, a cloud overshadowed him until his companions thought it was a painful punishment. Then he was called: "O Ayyub, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says:

Behold, I have drawn near to you, and I have never been far from you. Arise, present your excuse, speak of your innocence, dispute on your own behalf, gird up your loins, and stand as a mighty one disputing with a mighty one, if you are able. For none should dispute with Me except one mighty like Me. Your soul has deceived you, O Ayyub, into a matter that your strength cannot reach. Where were you when I created the earth and laid it on its foundation? Were you with Me, extending its edges? Did you know by what measure I determined it, or upon what I set its sides? Did water carry the earth by your obedience, or was the earth a covering for the water by Your wisdom? Where were you when I raised the sky as a roof in the air, not suspended by any cause from above, nor supported by any prop from below? Did your wisdom reach the point of making its light flow, or of moving its stars, or of making its night and day alternate by your command? Where were you when We sent forth the rivers and the seas were filled? Did your power restrain the waves of the seas within their boundaries? Or did your power open the wombs when their term was fulfilled? Where were you when I poured water upon the dust and set up the towering mountains? Do you know upon what I fixed them? By what weight did I weigh them? Or do you have an arm that can bear them? Or do you know from where the water comes that I send down from the sky? Or do you know from what I create the clouds? Or do you know where the treasuries of snow are? Or where are the mountains of hail? Or where is the store-house of the night by day [and the store-house of the day by night]? And where is the store-house of the wind? And in what language do the trees speak? And who placed intellects in the chests of men? And who split hearing and sight? And who made the angels submissive to His kingdom, and subdued the tyrants by His might? And who apportioned the provisions by His wisdom?"

This was in a long discourse of the signs of His power that He mentioned to Ayyub. Then Ayyub said:

"My station has become small, and all my tongue, my intellect and my understanding have been brought low, and my strength has grown weak before this matter that confronts me, O my God. I know that all that You have mentioned is the handiwork of Your hands and the governance of Your wisdom, and greater and more wondrous than that, and if You willed, You would act. Nothing can overpower You, and nothing is hidden from You, since affliction has come upon me. O my God, I spoke, and I did not control my tongue, and affliction was what made me speak. Would that the earth had split open for me so that I might go into it, and not have spoken anything that angers my Lord. Would that I had died of my grief in the severest of my trials before this. I spoke only so that You would excuse me, and I was silent only so that You would have mercy on me. A word slipped from me, and I will not return to it. I have placed my hand upon my mouth, bitten my tongue, and pressed my cheek into the dust. I seek refuge in You today from You, and I ask You to protect me from the severity of the affliction, so protect me. I seek Your help against Your punishment, so help me. I seek Your aid in my affair, so aid me. I rely upon You, so suffice me. I hold fast to You, so preserve me. And [I say to my wife]: you did not act justly. Had you been patient in affliction for eighty years as we were in ease for eighty years... By Allah, if Allah heals me, I will flog you one hundred lashes, because you commanded me to slaughter for other than Allah. Your food and your drink that you brought me are forbidden to me [or: it is forbidden to me] to taste anything of what you bring me after you said this to me. So go away from me, and I will not see you." So he drove her away, and she left. When Ayyub looked, and there was no food, no drink and no friend with him, he fell down in prostration and said:

﴿My Lord, indeed harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾

It was said to him: "Lift your head, for your prayer has been answered. Strike with your foot." He struck with his foot, and a spring gushed forth, and he bathed in it, and no outward trace of his disease remained except that it fell away, and his youth and beauty returned to him better than they had been. Then he struck with his foot again, and another spring gushed forth, and he drank from it, and no disease remained in his belly except that it came out. He stood up healthy and was clothed in a fine garment.

He began to look around, and he saw nothing of what he had possessed of family and wealth except that Allah had multiplied it for him. By Allah, it has been reported to us that the water in which he bathed scattered upon his chest as golden locusts, and he began to gather them in his hand. Then Allah revealed to him: "O Ayyub, did I not make you rich?" He said: "Yes, but this is Your blessing; who could be satisfied with it?" He went out and sat in an elevated place. Then his wife said: "Do you see? If he had driven me away to someone who would feed him? Shall I leave him to die of hunger and be lost, so that the beasts devour him?" She returned to him, but found no dung-heap and no state that she had known, and matters had changed. She began to wander where the dung-heap had been, weeping, and that was in Ayyub's sight. She was afraid of the man in the fine garment to approach him and ask him about him. So Ayyub called her and said:

"What do you want, O servant of Allah?"

She wept and said: "I wanted that afflicted man who was cast away on the dung-heap. I do not know whether he has perished or what has become of him." Ayyub said: "What was that from you?" She wept and said: "My husband." He said: "Would you recognise him if you saw him?" She said: "Could anyone who has seen him be hidden from me?" Then she began to look at him while being in awe of him, and then she said: "Surely he resembles most of Allah's creation to you when he was healthy." He said: "Indeed I am Ayyub, whom you commanded me to slaughter for Iblis. I obeyed Allah, disobeyed Satan, and called upon Allah, the Glorified, and He returned to me what you see."

Wahb said: Ayyub remained in affliction for three years. When Ayyub overcame Iblis and Iblis could not gain anything from him, Iblis appeared to his wife in a form unlike the form of the children of Adam in size, body, and beauty, upon a mount unlike the mounts of people, having greatness, splendor, and perfection. He said to her: "Are you the wife of Ayyub, this afflicted man?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know me?" She said: "No." He said: "I am the god of the earth, and I am the one who did to your companion what I did, because he worshipped the god of the heavens and left me, and so he angered me. If he had prostrated to me one single prostration, I would have returned to him and to you all the wealth and children you had, for it is with me." Then he showed them to her in the valley bottom where she had met him. Wahb said: I have also heard that he only said to her: "If your companion had eaten food without mentioning the name of Allah over it, he would have been healed of the affliction he has." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 17/66-67.]] And Allah knows best.

It is mentioned in some books that Iblis said to her: "Prostrate to me one prostration, and I will return to you the wealth and the children and heal your husband." She returned to Ayyub and informed him of what he had said to her [and what he had shown her]. [[Omitted from "B".]] He said: "The enemy of Allah has come to you to tempt you away from your religion." Then he swore that if Allah healed him, he would strike her one hundred lashes. At that point he said: "Harm has touched me" [referring to] Iblis's greed for her prostration to him, which violated my sanctity, and his calling her and me to disbelief. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, had mercy on Ayyub's wife for her patience with him in the affliction, and lightened it for her. He also wished to fulfil Ayyub's oath, so He commanded him to take a bundle containing one hundred small twigs and strike her with it in one blow, as Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it, and do not break your oath﴾ (38:44). It is also related that Iblis made a chest and put medicines in it, and sat on the road of his wife, treating people. Ayyub's wife passed by him and said: "[O shaykh], I have a sick man; shall I bring him to be treated?" He said: "Yes, [by Allah], I want nothing except that he say, when I have cured him, 'You have cured me.'" She mentioned this to Ayyub, and he said: "It is Iblis who has deceived you," and he swore that if Allah healed him, he would strike her one hundred lashes.

Wahb and others said: Ayyub's wife used to work for people and bring him his sustenance. When the affliction lengthened upon him and people grew weary of him, and no one employed her, she sought, one day, something to feed him, but found nothing. So she cut off a lock from her head and sold it for a loaf of bread and brought it to him. He said to her: "Where is your lock?" She informed him. [[Mentioned by al-Tabari: 17/66, from Wahb ibn Munabbih.]] At that point he said: ﴿Harm has touched me﴾.

Some people said: He only said that when worms reached his heart and tongue, and he feared they would make him cease from remembrance and reflection.

Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: He did not call upon Allah to remove it from him until three things had become apparent to him. The first: two friends came to him when news of him reached them; they came to him, and nothing remained of him except his eyes, and they saw a great matter, and said: "If you had a standing with Allah, this would not have befallen you." The second: his wife asked for food and found nothing to feed him, so she sold her forelock and brought him food. The third: Iblis's saying, "I will treat him on condition that he says, 'You have cured me.'"

It was also said: Iblis whispered to him that his wife had committed adultery, so she cut off her forelock. At that point his patience was overwhelmed, so he prayed and swore that he would strike her one hundred lashes. It was also said: its meaning is ﴿Harm has touched me﴾ from the gloating of enemies, to the extent that it is related that after he was healed he was asked: "What was harder for you in your affliction?" He said: "The gloating of the enemies." It was also said: he said that when a worm fell from his thigh and he put it back in its place.

[And he said: "Eat, for Allah has made me your food,"] so she bit him a bite whose pain exceeded everything he had suffered from the biting of the worms.

If it is said: Allah called him "patient," yet he displayed complaint and distress, by his saying: ﴿Indeed, harm has touched me﴾ and ﴿Satan has touched me with hardship and torment﴾ (38:41). It is said: this is not complaint; rather it is supplication, as evidenced by the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿So We responded to him﴾ (21:84). Moreover, distress is only in complaining to creatures; as for complaining to Allah, mighty and majestic, it is not distress nor abandonment of patience, as Ya'qub said: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah﴾ (12:86). Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: Likewise, whoever displays complaint to people while being content with the decree of Allah, this is not distress, as it is related that Jibril entered upon the Prophet ﷺ during his illness and said: "How do you find yourself?" He said: "I find myself troubled, and I find myself distressed." [[A fragment from a long hadith narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 3/139. al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 9/35, "In its chain is 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, who is abandoned in hadith."]]

And he said to 'A'isha when she said, "Oh my head!": "Nay, rather I say, 'Oh my head!'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Patients, chapter: What is permitted for the patient to say: "I have pain," or "Oh my head!"...: 10/123.]]

**The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 21, Verse 84:**

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿So We answered him and removed what afflicted him of harm﴾. The reason is that He said, "Strike the ground with your foot," so he struck it with his foot, and a spring of [water] gushed forth.[[Omitted from "ب".]] He commanded him to bathe in it, and he did so, and every disease that was on his outward body went away. Then he walked forty paces, and He commanded him to strike the ground with his foot once more, and he did so, and a spring of cold water gushed forth. He commanded him, and he drank from it, and every disease that was within his body went away. He became like the healthiest and most beautiful of men.

﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them﴾. Scholars differed regarding this. Ibn Mas'ud, Qatadah, Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and most of the exegetes said: Allah, Exalted and Majestic, returned to him his family and his children in their own persons, having brought them back to life for him, and gave him the like of them along with them. This is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.[[Al-Tabari transmitted these sayings: 17/72-73.]]

Al-Hasan said: Allah gave him the like of his wealth from its offspring, which Allah had returned to him, and his family. What supports this is what al-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas related, that Allah, Exalted and Majestic, restored to the woman her youth, and she bore him twenty-six males.[[Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/660, attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir, through the route of Juwaybir from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas.]]

Wahb said: He had seven daughters and three sons.

Ibn Yasar said: He had seven sons and seven daughters.

It is related from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): He had two andars (threshing-floors), one for wheat and one for barley. Allah, Exalted and Majestic, sent two clouds, one of which poured gold onto the wheat threshing-floor, and the other poured silver onto the barley threshing-floor, until it overflowed.[[Al-Hakim transmitted it: 2/581-582, and authenticated it according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim.]]

It is also related that Allah, Exalted, sent an angel to him and said: "Your Lord sends you His greetings for your patience. Go out to your threshing-floor." So he went out to it, and Allah sent upon him locusts of gold. One flew off and he followed it and returned it to his threshing-floor. The angel said to him: "Are you not content with what is in your threshing-floor?" He said: "This is one of the blessings of my Lord, and I am never satisfied with His blessing."[[Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/660, attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir, through the route of Juwaybir from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas.]]

Ḥassān ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmish al-Ziyadi informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us, Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayrah informed us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While Ayyub was bathing naked, a swarm of golden locusts fell upon him, and Ayyub began gathering them into his garment. His Lord called out to him, 'O Ayyub, did I not make you wealthy enough to be free of what you see?' He said: 'Yes, by Your might, my Lord, but there is no independence for me from Your blessing.'"[[Al-Bukhari transmitted it in the Book of the Prophets, chapter: "The saying of Allah: (And Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, 'Indeed, adversity has touched me...')": 6/420, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/7.]]

Some people said: Allah gave Ayyub in this world the like of his family who had perished. As for those who had perished, they were not returned to him in this world.[[Al-Tabari mentioned it: 17/72.]] Ikrimah said: It was said to Ayyub: "Your family is for you in the Hereafter. If you wish, We will hasten them for you in this world, and if you wish, they will be for you in the Hereafter, and We will give you the like of them in this world." He said: "Let them be for me in the Hereafter, and let the like of them be given to me in this world."[[Al-Tabari transmitted it: 17/72.]] According to this, the meaning of the verse is: "And We gave him his family in the Hereafter and the like of them with them in this world." By "family" he means the children.

﴿A mercy from Us﴾, i.e., a blessing from Us. ﴿And a reminder for the worshippers﴾, i.e., an admonition and a lesson for them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Isma'il﴾, meaning the son of Ibrahim (Ibrahim), ﴿and Idris﴾, who is Akhnukh (Akhnukh), ﴿and Dhu'l-Kifl; all were of the patient﴾ in obeying God's command. They differed concerning Dhu'l-Kifl.

ʿAtaʾ said: A prophet among the prophets of the Children of Israel, to whom God revealed, "I intend to take your soul, so present your kingdom to the Children of Israel. Whoever guarantees to you that he will pray at night without ceasing, fast by day without breaking the fast, and judge between people without becoming angry, then hand your kingdom over to him." He did so. A young man stood up and said, "I will guarantee this for you," so he took on the guarantee and fulfilled it. God thanked him for it and made him a prophet, and so he was named Dhu'l-Kifl. [[See Zad al-Masir: 5/379–380.]]

Mujahid said: When al-Yasaʿ grew old, he said, "[If] I appoint a man over the people to govern them during my lifetime, so that I may see how he governs." He gathered the people and said, "Whoever will take on from me three things, I will appoint him: he fasts by day, stands in prayer by night, and does not become angry." A man whom people looked down upon stood up and said, "I will." He dismissed him that day, then said the same thing the next day, and the people were silent. That man stood up again and said, "I will," so he appointed him. Then Iblis came to him in the form of a feeble old man at the time he lay down for the midday rest, for he would not sleep at night or by day except for that nap. He knocked on the door, and he said, "Who is this?" He said, "An old, oppressed man." So he got up, opened the door, and the man said, "Between me and my people there is a dispute, and they have wronged me, and they did such-and-such," and he kept prolonging it until the time of afternoon came and the midday rest had passed. He said, "When you go out, come to me, and I will take your right for you." The old man left, and [the judge] went out and sat in his council, looking to see whether he would see the old man, but he did not see him. He got up to search for him. When the next day came, he sat judging between people and waited for him, but did not see him. When he returned to the midday rest and lay down, [the old man] came and knocked on the door. He said, "Who is this?" He said, "The oppressed old man." So he opened the door for him and said, "Did I not tell you, when you sit, come to me?" He said, "They are the most wicked of people: when they know you are sitting, they say, 'We will give you your right,' and when I rise, they deny me." He said, "Go, and when you go out, come to me." The midday rest passed him by and he went out and kept looking, but did not see him, and drowsiness overcame him. He said to some of his household, "Do not let anyone come near this door until I sleep, for sleep has overcome me." When that hour came, [the old man] arrived, but the man did not give him permission. When he had grown weary, he looked and saw an opening in the house, so he climbed through it, and there he was inside the house knocking on the door from within. He woke up and said, "O so-and-so, did I not command you?" He said, "As for my side, you were not attacked; look from where you were attacked." He went to the door and found it locked as he had locked it, and the man was with him in the house. He said, "Do you sleep while the disputants are at your door?" He recognized him and said, "Enemy of God?" He said, "Yes, you wearied me, so I did what you see, to anger you, and God protected you." He was named Dhu'l-Kifl because he took on a matter and fulfilled it. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 17/74.]]

It is also said: Iblis came to him and said, "I have a creditor who delays paying me, and I would like you to stand with me and collect my right from him." So he went with him, until when they were in the market, he left him and departed. It is also narrated that he apologized to him and said, "My companion has fled."

It is also said: Dhu'l-Kifl was a man who undertook to pray one hundred rak'ahs every night until God took him, and he fulfilled it.

They differed as to whether he was a prophet. Some of them said he was a prophet. [[Ibn Kathir said: 3/191 (. . . As for Dhu'l-Kifl, the apparent sense of the context is that he is only mentioned alongside the prophets if he was a prophet. Others said: he was only a righteous man, a just king and an equitable judge. Ibn Jarir hesitated on this, and God knows best). Ibn Jarir said: 17/73 (. . . By Dhu'l-Kifl is meant a man who undertook a matter from some people, either from a prophet or from one of the righteous kings, by some deed, and another after him carried it out. God praised him for the excellence of his fulfilling what he had undertaken, and made him among those counted among His servants, along with praise for his patience in obeying God. What we have said concerning his affair is what has come in reports from the early scholars).]] Others said: he is Ilyas. Others said: he is Zakariyya. Abu Musa said: he was not a prophet, but was a righteous servant. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 17/75.]]

﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy﴾: meaning the blessings Allah bestowed upon them of prophethood, and He brought them to Him in Paradise with reward. ﴿Indeed, they were among the righteous.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Dhu'n-Nun﴾, i.e., remember the companion of the fish, who is Yunus ibn Matta, ﴿when he went off in anger﴾. The scholars differed concerning its meaning.

Al-Dahhak said: "Angry with his people." This is the narration of al-Awfi and others from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Yunus and his people lived in Palestine, and a king invaded them and took captive nine and a half tribes, leaving one and a half tribes. Allah revealed to the prophet Sha'ya': "Go to Hizqil the king and tell him that he should send a strong prophet, for I will cast terror into the hearts of those (enemies) so that they will send the Children of Israel with him." The king said to him, "Whom do you suggest?" There were five prophets in his kingdom. Yunus said, "He is strong and trustworthy." So the king summoned Yunus and ordered him to set out. Yunus said to him, "Has Allah commanded you to send me out?" He said, "No." He said, "Has He named me to you?" He said, "No." He said, "There are other strong prophets here besides me." They insisted upon him, so he left them angry at the prophet, the king, and his people. He went to the Sea of Rum and boarded it. [Cf. Zad al-Masir: 5/381.]

Qatadah ibn... [translation continues]

And 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and a group said: He left his people angry at his Lord, when He lifted the punishment from his people after He had threatened them. He disliked being among a people who had tested him with unfulfilled promises regarding what he had threatened them with, and he was ashamed before them, and he did not know the reason for which the punishment was lifted. His anger was out of aversion to appearing to have broken his promise, and that he would be called a liar, not out of dislike for the judgment of Allah, exalted is He. [Previously cited in the commentary on Surah Yunus.]

In some reports, it was the custom of his people to kill anyone who had been tested as a liar. He feared they would kill him when the punishment did not come at the appointed time, so he became angry. The word "mughadabah" here is like the form "mufa'alah" that arises from one party, as in "musafarah" and "mu'aqabah," so the meaning of His saying "angry" (mughadiban) is "wrathful" (ghadban).

Al-Hasan said: He was angry with his Lord, exalted and mighty is He, because He commanded him to go to his people to warn them of His might and call them to Him. He asked his Lord to give him respite so he could prepare to set out to them, but it was said to him that the matter was quicker than that, until he asked to be given respite only long enough to take a sandal to wear, and he was not given respite. [Cf. al-Tabari: 17/77.] There was narrowness in his character, [so he went off angry].

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Jibril came to Yunus and said, "Set out to the people of Nineveh and warn them." He said, "Let me find an animal to ride." He said, "The matter is more urgent than that." So he became angry and went off to the ship.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Yunus ibn Matta was a righteous servant, but there was narrowness in his character. When the heavy burdens of prophethood were placed upon him, he buckled beneath them as a young camel [rabu'] buckles under a heavy load, so he threw them from his hand and fled out from under them. For this reason Allah did not include him among the steadfast messengers (ulu al-'azm), and He said to His Prophet [Muhammad ﷺ]: ﴿So be patient as the steadfast messengers were patient﴾ (al-Ahqaf: 35), and He said: ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾ (al-Qalam: 48).

[Al-Tabari, 17/77–78, cited both of these opinions, then said: "Neither of these two opinions describes the Prophet of Allah Yunus, may Allah's blessings be upon him, with anything except that it is less than what those who said 'he went off angry at his people' described him with, because his going away from his people angry with them, when Allah, exalted is He, had commanded him to remain among them to convey His message and warn them of His might and punishment for their refusal to believe in Him and to obey Him, there is no doubt that there is something wrong in it. And had he not committed what those who described him said he committed, a sin, Allah, exalted is His remembrance, would not have punished him with the punishment He mentioned in His Book and described him with the description He gave, saying to His Prophet ﷺ: 'And do not be like the companion of the fish when he called out while suppressing grief' and saying: 'Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy. Had he not been of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.'"]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he thought that We would not decree against him﴾: i.e., that We would not decide upon punishment. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi, and it is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. It is said: "Qaddara Allah al-shay' taqdiran" and "qadara yaqdiru qadran" have the same meaning, and from it is His saying: ﴿We have decreed death among you﴾ (al-Waqi'ah: 60) in the recitation of the one who reads it with a light (takhfif) pronunciation. The evidence for this interpretation is the recitation of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and al-Zuhri: ﴿And he thought that We would not decree against him﴾ with a doubled consonant (tashdid). 'Ata' and many scholars said: Its meaning is "he thought that We would not restrict him in imprisonment," from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾ (al-Ra'd: 26), i.e., restricts. Ibn Zayd said: It is an interrogative, meaning: "Did he think that He would be unable to overpower his Lord, so that He would have no power over him?" Ya'qub read yuqdara [with a dammah on the ya'] in the passive, lightly pronounced.

It is related from al-Hasan who said: It reached me that when Yunus committed the sin, he went off angry at his Lord, and Satan led him astray until he thought that We would not decide against him. He had previously had a good record and worship, but Allah refused to leave him to Satan, so He cast him into the belly of the fish, where he remained for forty days and nights. ['Ata' said seven days.] [And it was said: three days.] It was also said that the fish carried him a distance of six thousand years. It was said: It reached with him to the boundaries of the seventh earth, and he repented to his Lord, exalted is He, in the belly of the fish, reflected upon himself and said: ﴿There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers﴾, when I disobeyed You and did what I did. So I will not worship other than You. Then Allah brought him out of the belly of the fish by His mercy. The earlier interpretations are more fitting for the state of the prophets: that he went off angry at his people or at the king. ﴿And he called out within the darknesses﴾, i.e., the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish: ﴿That there is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.﴾

It is related from Abu Hurayrah, traced back to the Prophet (marfu'): Allah revealed to the fish, "Take him, but do not scratch his flesh or break his bone." So it took him and plunged with him down to its dwelling place in the sea. When it reached the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself, "What is this?" Allah revealed to him: "This is the glorification of the creatures of the sea." He said: So he glorified Allah while in the belly of the fish, and the angels heard his glorification. They said, "O our Lord, we hear a faint sound from a strange land." In another narration: "a known sound from an unknown place." He said: "That is My servant Yunus who disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the fish." They said: "The righteous servant from whom a righteous deed has ascended to You every day and night?" He said: "Yes." So they interceded for him. At that point He commanded the fish, and it cast him onto the shore, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So We threw him onto the barren land while he was ill﴾ (al-Saffat: 145).

﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy﴾: meaning the blessings Allah bestowed upon them of prophethood, and He brought them to Him in Paradise with reward. ﴿Indeed, they were among the righteous.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Dhu'n-Nun﴾, i.e., remember the companion of the fish, who is Yunus ibn Matta, ﴿when he went off in anger﴾. The scholars differed concerning its meaning.

The king said to him, "Whom do you suggest?" There were five prophets in his kingdom. Yunus said, "He is strong and trustworthy." So the king summoned Yunus and ordered him to set out. Yunus said to him, "Has Allah commanded you to send me out?" He said, "No." He said, "Has He named me to you?" He said, "No." He said, "There are other strong prophets here besides me." They insisted upon him, so he left them angry at the prophet, the king, and his people. He went to the Sea of Rum and boarded it. [Cf. Zad al-Masir: 5/381.]

So it took him and plunged with him down to its dwelling place in the sea. When it reached the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself, "What is this?" They said, "O our Lord, we hear a faint sound from a strange land." In another narration: "a known sound from an unknown place." They said: "The righteous servant from whom a righteous deed has ascended to You every day and night?" He said: "Yes." So they interceded for him. Therefore, His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So We answered him﴾, meaning We responded to him, ﴿and We delivered him from the distress﴾, from those darknesses, ﴿and thus do We deliver the believers﴾ from every affliction when they call upon Us and seek Our help.

Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim, in the transmission of Abu Bakr, read "nunji" with a single nun, a doubled jim, and a sukun on the ya', because it is written in the Mushaf with a single nun. The grammarians (nuhat) differed concerning this reading. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verse 97:

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿And the true promise draws near﴾, meaning the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah). Al-Farra' and a group said: the waw in His saying "wa-iqtaraba" [is superfluous (muqhamah), so its meaning is: until, when Gog and Magog are opened, the true promise draws near], as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when they both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead, and We called to him﴾ (al-Saffat: 103), meaning "We called to him". The evidence for this is what is related from Hudhayfah, who said: "If a man were to acquire a colt after the emergence of Gog and Magog, he would not ride it until the Hour is established." [Related by al-Tabari: 17/92.]

Others said: it is not permissible to drop the waw. They made the answer (jawab) of "until, when they are opened" to be in His saying "O woe to us", so the meaning of the verse becomes: until, when Gog and Magog are opened and the true promise draws near, they will say: "O woe to us! We were heedless of this." This is supported by His saying: ﴿Then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾. In His saying "hiya" there are three aspects:

The first: it is a pronoun referring back to "the eyes" (al-absar), and then "the eyes" is made explicit as a clarification, meaning: "then the eyes are staring fixedly, the eyes of those who disbelieved".

The second: "hiya" is a pronoun of support (imad), as in His saying: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded﴾ (al-Hajj: 46).

The third: the complete sentence ends at His saying "hiya", in the sense of "then it is exposed (barizah)", meaning, because of its nearness, as if it were present. Then he begins: ﴿The eyes of those who disbelieved stare fixedly﴾, with the predicate placed before the subject, its meaning being: "the eyes of those who disbelieved are staring fixedly". Al-Kalbi said: The eyes of the disbelievers stare fixedly, hardly blinking, because of the intensity and terror of that Day. They will say, ﴿O woe to us! We were heedless of this﴾ Day, ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾ by placing worship in other than its proper place.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 21, verses 98–101:

﴿Indeed, you﴾, O polytheists, ﴿and what you worship besides Allah﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿are the fuel of Hell﴾, i.e., its firewood. Mujahid and Qatadah said: its kindling. In the dialect of the people of Yemen, *haṣab* (fuel) means firewood. Ikrimah said: it means firewood in the language of Abyssinia. al-Dahhak said: it means they will be hurled into the Fire as pebbles are thrown. The root of *haṣab* is throwing, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿We sent against them a violent wind﴾ (al-Qamar: 34), meaning a wind that pelts them with stones. Ali ibn Abi Talib recited it as *ḥaṭab Jahannam* (the firewood of Hell). ﴿You will be entering it﴾, i.e., you will be entering it.

﴿If these had been gods﴾, meaning the idols, ﴿in truth, they would not have entered it﴾, i.e., those who worshipped them would not have entered the Fire. ﴿And all of them will abide therein forever﴾, meaning the worshipper and the worshipped.

﴿For them therein will be groaning, and they therein will not hear﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: regarding this verse, when those who will remain forever in the Fire are left there, they are placed in coffins of fire, and those coffins are placed inside other coffins, and then those coffins inside other coffins [[The words in brackets are an addition from manuscript "B".]], upon which are nails of fire. So they hear nothing, and none of them sees that anyone in the Fire is being punished other than himself. Then He made an exception, saying:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾. Some scholars said: here *inna* carries the meaning of *illa* (except), i.e., except those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, meaning happiness and the beautiful promise of Paradise. ﴿Those will be kept far away from it﴾. It was said: the verse is general concerning everyone for whom happiness has preceded from Allah. Most exegetes said: by this is meant everyone who was worshipped besides Allah while being obedient to Allah and displeased with the worship of those who worship him. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the Masjid while the chieftains of Quraysh were in al-Hatim around the Ka'bah, and there were three hundred and sixty idols around it. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith met him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾, the three verses. Then he stood up, and Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Sahmi came, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira informed him of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to them. Abd Allah said: By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued him down.
